title: How a Single-Chain Polystyrene Nanoparticle Dictates alpha-Synuclein Adsorption and Intramolecular beta-Sheet Nucleation.
authors: Wang, Kang; Gong, Shuai; Sheng, Yifeng; Shen, Lei
journal: Langmuir : the ACS journal of surfaces and colloids
one_liner_zh: 该文用增强采样MD模拟研究聚苯乙烯纳米颗粒尺寸如何调控α-突触核蛋白的吸附与分子内β-折叠成核，虽对象涉及纳米塑料，但核心是蛋白质构象转变的结构计算问题，方法为物理模拟，可迁移至蛋白构象采样研究。
abstract: A growing number of studies have detected nanoplastics, particularly polystyrene (PS) nanoparticles, in human blood and various critical tissues. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms by which their physical size modulates the aggregation of disease-related proteins remain poorly understood. Here, using well-tempered metadynamics simulations, we demonstrate that single-chain PS nanoparticles with a degree of polymerization N collapse into spherical globules in water, following a scaling law of radius of gyration Rg  approximately  N1/3, and that their size critically determines the conformational fate of alpha-synuclein (alphaS), a key protein in Parkinson's disease. Within our single-chain simulation framework, we observe a sensitive size-dependent transition regime around N = 75 to 80 (Rg = 1.14 to 1.16 nm), where PS nanoparticles transition from insufficient surface area to a threshold capable of encapsulating the alphaS chain. The partially exposed protein chain subsequently folds into stable intramolecular beta-sheet domains, representing the initial nucleation step toward amyloid aggregation. Conversely, nanoparticles with N >/= 80 (Rg >/= 1.16 nm) present a sufficiently large hydrophobic surface to completely encapsulate alphaS through dominant hydrophobic and pi-pi interactions, effectively suppressing the intramolecular beta-sheet nucleation. These findings reveal that smaller nanoplastics may inadvertently promote protein misfolding, which may implicitly lower the likelihood of downstream intermolecular aggregation. Our work establishes a quantitative, size-dependent hazard principle for nanoplastic neurotoxicity and provides a molecular foundation for assessing the risk of environmentally derived nanoparticles in synucleinopathies.
abstract_zh: 越来越多的研究在人体血液及多种关键组织中检测到纳米塑料，尤其是聚苯乙烯（PS）纳米颗粒。然而，其物理尺寸如何调控疾病相关蛋白聚集的分子机制仍知之甚少。在此，利用温和偏置元动力学模拟，我们证明聚合度为N的单链PS纳米颗粒在水中塌缩为球形小球，遵循回转半径Rg约等于N1/3的标度律，且其尺寸关键性地决定α-突触核蛋白（alphaS）——帕金森病中的关键蛋白——的构象命运。在我们的单链模拟框架内，我们观察到在N = 75至80（Rg = 1.14至1.16 nm）附近存在一个敏感的尺寸依赖性转变区间，在此区间内，PS纳米颗粒从表面积不足转变为能够包封alphaS链的阈值。部分暴露的蛋白链随后折叠成稳定的分子内β-折叠结构域，代表向淀粉样聚集的初始成核步骤。相反，N ≥ 80（Rg ≥ 1.16 nm）的纳米颗粒具有足够大的疏水表面，通过主导的疏水相互作用和π-π相互作用完全包封alphaS，有效抑制分子内β-折叠成核。这些发现揭示，较小的纳米塑料可能无意中促进蛋白错误折叠，这可能间接降低下游分子间聚集的可能性。我们的工作为纳米塑料神经毒性建立了定量的、尺寸依赖的危害原则，并为评估环境来源纳米颗粒在突触核蛋白病中的风险提供了分子基础。
